## Analytics should help someone decide what to do next.

The useful part of analytics is not the model, dashboard, database, or AI workflow by itself. It is the clearer decision, more reliable process, or better-designed system that those tools make possible.

I work with organizations that have important questions, fragmented data, recurring manual work, or analytic products that need to become more useful, repeatable, and maintainable.

## Get more value from the data you already collect.

Small organizations often have meaningful program data but limited time, staff, or budget to turn it into useful reporting and insight. I offer a **Nonprofit Analytics Quick Start** designed to identify practical improvements without requiring a large consulting engagement.

We can review the spreadsheets, forms, reports, grant requirements, and recurring processes you already use; identify a small set of useful measures; find gaps or unnecessary manual work; and choose one or two improvements that can create immediate value.

**Good fits include:** grant and board reporting, program metrics, outcome tracking, recurring spreadsheet workflows, surveys, data visualization, and simple reporting automation.

[Learn about the Nonprofit Analytics Quick Start →](services.qmd#nonprofit-analytics-quick-start){.btn .btn-primary}
:::

## The tool comes after the problem.

::: {.principle-grid}
::: {.principle}
### 01 · Start with the decision
Define what someone needs to know, decide, or change before deciding what to build.
:::
::: {.principle}
### 02 · Design with stakeholders
Understand how people work, what they trust, and what will make a solution usable in practice.
:::
::: {.principle}
### 03 · Build for repeatability
Prefer transparent, documented workflows that can be validated, updated, and handed off.
:::
::: {.principle}
### 04 · Make implementation part of the work
A technically correct solution that never gets adopted is not a successful analytics project.
:::
:::
:::
